forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

findings.paper_title: 061126 - Report - YNYCA Budget Monitoring Report - Q2 2026-27
findings.headline: The 2026/27 budget has risen from £184.658m to £219.507m after £34.848m of adjustments, including £23.783m of 2025/26 carry forward.
findings.detail: Adjustments since February 2026 include £8.650m of confirmed additional grant funding, £0.775m of new approved programmes and £0.612m of adjustments between capital and revenue. A further £2.210m of changes were made since Q1, and £2.736m of additional budget is requested in Section 10.
findings.matters: A budget that has grown by almost a fifth in-year, largely from carry forward and grant, is one that finance directors and lenders will want to track against the original approval.
findings.figures: £184.658m original budget; £34.848m adjustments; £219.507m latest budget; £23.783m carry forward; £8.650m additional grant; £2.210m Q1 to Q2 increase; £2.736m further requested

findings.paper_title: 061126 - Report - YNYCA Budget Monitoring Report - Q2 2026-27
findings.headline: Budgeted reserves usage is forecast to fall by £2.707m.
findings.detail: The paper reports reserves transfers at a latest budget of £10.581m, with a forecast of £7.874m. It cites the reduction as one of the three components of the £4.947m forecast underspend.
findings.matters: A lower draw on budgeted reserves than planned directly affects the level of reserves remaining, which lenders and finance directors track.
findings.figures: £2.707m reduction in budgeted reserves usage; transfer to/from reserves latest budget £10.581m; forecast £7.874m
findings.quote: A forecast reduction of £2.707m of budgeted reserves usage.

findings.paper_title: 061126 - Report - YNYCA Budget Monitoring Report - Q2 2026-27
findings.headline: Transport capital is forecast £0.815m under budget, and officers are scoping a proposal to carry the funding into 2027/28 for bus stop improvements.
findings.detail: The paper describes this as the only net capital underspend outside Housing. Options to carry it forward are still being scoped, and no decision has been taken.
findings.matters: A capital underspend being rolled forward to a named purpose, rather than returned, is a funding decision that finance officers at other councils running bus programmes may encounter.
findings.figures: £0.815m Transport capital underspend; Transport capital latest budget £102.337m; forecast outturn £101.522m
findings.quote: Currently scoping is underway on a proposal to carry forward the funding to 2027/28 for use towards bus stops improvements.

findings.paper_title: 061126 - Report - YNYCA Budget Monitoring Report - Q2 2026-27
findings.headline: Transport revenue is forecast £0.565m over budget and Skills and Workforce £0.477m over budget.
findings.detail: The Transport overspend relates to the Bus Delivery Review, which will use investment income as a funding mechanism. The Skills overspend arises because Bootcamps were not budgeted in line with academic years. The paper says that as claims are made in arrears, the Skills overspend will be fully mitigated.
findings.matters: Overspends in the same year as a wider underspend, funded from investment income, show how a council is moving spending between programmes and funding streams.
findings.figures: Transport overspend £0.565m; Skills and Workforce overspend £0.477m; Healthy & Thriving Communities overspend £0.217m
findings.quote: Overspends should be noted against Transport (£0.565m) and Skills and Workforce (£0.477m).

findings.paper_title: 061126 - Report - YNYCA Budget Monitoring Report - Q2 2026-27
findings.headline: Revenue Programmes are forecast £2.913m under budget, with the full balance to be transferred to reserves at year end.
findings.detail: The Carbon Negative Region (Energy Generator Accelerator, £0.776m) and Inclusive Economic Growth (Local Growth Fund £0.943m, Community Wealth Building £0.400m) underspends account for most of the total. The Community Wealth Building project is now being delivered over three years rather than one, and the Local Growth Fund has delayed expenditure while a delivery plan is devised.
findings.matters: Underspends moved into reserves to fund delayed programmes show how a council is carrying delivery risk on its balance sheet, which is relevant to anyone assessing reserve adequacy.
findings.figures: £2.913m revenue underspend; £0.776m Energy Generator Accelerator; £0.943m Local Growth Fund; £0.400m Community Wealth Building; £68.629m latest revenue budget
findings.quote: Of which, the full balance is forecast to be transferred to reserves at the year end.

dossier.name: York and North Yorkshire Combined Authority

daily_post.headline: Combined Authority lacked risk management arrangements and approved Risk Management Policy in its first three months, with no performance monitoring produced
daily_post.lead: Without formal risk management and performance monitoring arrangements, the Authority cannot demonstrate it can navigate operating uncertainties, manage financial risks, or assure delivery of its strategic objectives.
